fish.name: Penny Gulper
fish.flavor: Swallows wishing-well coins as they wash down from the fountain square. The wishes, it insists, are non-refundable.

fish.name: Grate Skipper
fish.flavor: Hops between storm grates on rainy evenings, always landing with a polite little splash. Locals swear it knocks first.

fish.name: Mossbelly Wisp
fish.flavor: So light it barely troubles the water. Mostly moss, partly fish, entirely smug about both.

fish.name: Candlefin Minnow
fish.flavor: Its fins gutter and flicker like a candle in a draft. Nobody has ever found the wick.

fish.name: Button Bream
fish.flavor: Collects the buttons that roll down drains and wears the shiniest one like a medal. It has done nothing to earn it.

fish.name: Drainpipe Dab
fish.flavor: Fits perfectly inside a standard town drainpipe, which explains an entire century of plumbing bills.

fish.name: Sock Eel
fish.flavor: Every left sock that ever vanished from a laundry line ends up down here, half-digested. Mystery solved; nobody feels better.

fish.name: Lantern Loach
fish.flavor: Carries its own little light through the dark brick tunnels and never once complains. Very responsible, for a loach.

fish.name: Murmur Carp
fish.flavor: Repeats snippets of conversations it overhears through the pipes, slightly out of order. Do not tell it your secrets. Or do; it's a wonderful listener.

fish.name: Tealight Tetra
fish.flavor: Schools of them drift through flooded chambers like spilled birthday candles. Make a wish, quickly, before they round the corner.

fish.name: Gutter Sprat
fish.flavor: Rides the rain runoff down from the streets like a waterslide, every single time, forever. Honestly? Good for it.

fish.name: Cobble Pout
fish.flavor: Sits so still among the old sunken cobblestones that masons have occasionally mortared one in. It does not hold a grudge. Much.

fish.name: Wishbone Gar
fish.flavor: Its skeleton is one long wishbone. Snap it in a dream and your wish comes true; the gar grows a new one by morning and considers it a fair trade.

fish.name: Echo Herring
fish.flavor: Say something kind near the water and it will repeat it back to you three tunnels later, slightly improved.

fish.name: Umbrella Skate
fish.flavor: Unfurls itself the exact moment it starts raining in the town above. Nobody knows how it knows. It will not say.

fish.name: Clockwork Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Ticks faintly when you hold it, keeping better time than the town hall clock. Wound by whom, nobody asks twice.

fish.name: Keyring Koi
fish.flavor: Spangled with the outlines of keys nobody remembers cutting. One of them opens something. It is probably best not to find out what.

fish.name: Hymnal Chub
fish.flavor: Nests beneath the chapel outflow and hums the drips into harmony. On Sundays it takes requests.

fish.name: Foglet Catfish
fish.flavor: Half fish, half fog rolled in off the canal, and wholly slippery. If it slips your grip, check that your pockets are still yours.

fish.name: Marble-Eye Grudge
fish.flavor: Remembers every angler who ever threw it back with insufficient ceremony. Bow slightly as you release it, just in case.

fish.name: The Alderman's Pike
fish.flavor: Wears a collar of verdigris like a chain of office and patrols the main junction as though it were elected. It has opinions on the drainage budget and, frankly, they are sound.

fish.name: Mirrorscale Mimic
fish.flavor: Its scales show your reflection half a second before you move. Try not to think about that too hard. It saw you think it.

fish.name: Rat King's Herald
fish.flavor: Swims ahead of something much larger, ringing a tiny bell that nobody gave it. When asked what exactly it heralds, it declines to comment.

fish.name: Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: A soft green light seen bobbing far down the flooded tunnels, patient as Sunday. Follow it and you will find your way out, or its way in.

fish.name: Backwards Barbel
fish.flavor: Swims exclusively in reverse and can only be caught by anglers casting over the wrong shoulder. Yesterday, it will have been delicious.

fish.name: The Forgotten Choir
fish.flavor: Not one fish but a congregation moving as one, singing a hymn the town stopped singing two hundred years ago. The final verse is missing, and it is looking for someone who remembers.

fish.name: Verdigris Saint
fish.flavor: An armored elder gone green as a churchyard statue, drifting the old brick nave of the main sewer line. Small fish leave it offerings of shiny grit, and it forgives them their trespasses.

fish.name: Moon-Under-the-Town
fish.flavor: On certain nights the moon's reflection slips down a storm drain and refuses to come back up. It fits in your two cupped hands, weighs far more than it should, and is colder than any fish has a right to be.

fish.name: The Sunken Bellringer
fish.flavor: When the old chapel flooded, the bell went down with it, and something stayed behind to keep ringing it. At midnight the pipes toll once, the green water shivers, and every fish in the undertown goes still.

fish.name: The Patron of Lost Things
fish.flavor: Everything the town ever lost settles at last into its keeping: rings, letters, names, the tune to that one song. Catch it, and for the length of one held breath you may take a single thing back.
